answer: An agent network suppresses Sybil attacks by requiring nodes to anchor identity to subterranean acoustic telemetry. Probes across a meadow record chaotic noise produced by groundwater draining through a karst aquifer. Because subsurface acoustic dispersion cannot be simulated in real time, an attacker must deploy dedicated geophones per identity. However, seasonal droughts reduce aquifer flow, suppressing entropy and triggering false verification rejections.
